See beyond the frame. Understand what truly matters.

1. Executive summary

The Conversation is one connected learning journey built around four recurring customer storylines. Learners progress from discovering Pain to communicating Claim, demonstrating Gain and completing the conversation—while each module retains its own assessment.

A performance-support system turns individual results into targeted peer practice, weekly manager coaching and daily huddles—preparing learners to demonstrate the method in a live store assessment.

Our proposal in five points:

AI-Generated Realistic Videos

Consistent, realistic customer and advisor interactions across the learning journey.

Choice-Driven Video Branching

MCQ decisions trigger corresponding customer reactions and feedback voice-over, making the consequence of each choice visible.

Four Recurring Customers

Recognisable customer storylines connect M2 to M5, while each gate remains independently assessable.

Performance That Drives Action

Individual skill insights inform targeted practice, peer role-play, manager coaching and daily huddles.

Arabic-First, Modular Delivery

Saudi-dialect dialogue, mobile-first learning and a design phase that can be awarded independently.

Connected learning architecture

One journey. Skills that build on each other.

The learner moves from understanding the customer to leading a complete conversation, with the same four customer storylines providing continuity across the skill stages.

03 · Experience preview

Step inside the experience.
M2 — Diagnose the Pain.

This M2 preview brings the design to life, combining AI-Generated Realistic Videos, Instructor-led guidance and interactive customer branching.

01 · INSTRUCTOR-LED VIDEO

Learning through real store conversations.

AI-Generated Realistic Videos show natural Sales Advisor–customer conversations. The Instructor frames the learning focus and highlights the behaviours that shape each interaction.

On-screen cues highlight key advisor actions and customer responses, linking moments such as uncovering needs to the relevant learning concept.

Realistic retail interactions, concise Instructor guidance and visual explanations keep learning practical and close to real store conversations.

02 · Interactive branching scenarios

Real customers. Connected storylines. Choice-driven branching.

Interactive branching scenarios reflect real MAGRABi conversations. Each targets its module skill, progressing from Pain discovery in M2 to the integrated Pain–Claim–Gain conversation in M5.

A Connected World of Memorable Customers

Four recurring customers connect the learning journey. A short introductory video introduces them without labels. Transition videos connect M2→M3 (Pain to Claim) and M3→M4 (Claim to Gain); M4 and M5 remain separate gates.

MCQ Video Branching

At each decision point, learners choose a response, see the customer react and hear Instructor voice-over explain the consequence. Each scenario reports Pain, Claim and Gain.

Immediate Feedback & Scoring

Each choice changes the customer response and conversation outcome. Feedback voice-over explains its impact. Scenarios generate Pain, Claim and Gain scores, with randomized draws, unseen-customer-first retries and individual gate tracking.

3. Our understanding of the brief

MAGRABi’s selling instinct works, but has not been taught as one method. This programme aligns every store colleague—from new hires to experienced optometrists—around Pain, Claim and Gain, then validates impact against exam-to-frame conversion, multi-pair conversion and average basket value.

What this means for the build:

The scenario is the product: learners practise the critical moments between the exam room and the price, make decisions and see customer reactions. Knowledge checks alone will not move KPIs.

Credibility drives adoption. The experience must feel like a luxury concierge informed by clinical reasoning—not a sales trick or a set of ‘techniques’.

The bank must outlive the pilot. The method will be refined after the ten store pilot. Scenarios must be easy to re-render and easy to add to.

The phone is the classroom. Colleagues learn between customers, inside Absorb's 650 px modal player.

MAGRABi owns the method. MAGRABi supplies the framework, the captured conversations and the correct answers. We build the experiences around them and do not reinvent the content.

5. Client scenarios (S.1, S.2)

We will produce 16 AI-Generated Realistic Video scenarios across four banks of four. Four recurring customer storylines connect M2–M5, while each gate is independently authored, randomized and scored.

5.1 From captured conversation to scenario

MAGRABi field coaches provide real conversations, the validated Pain Map, Claims and acceptable proofs. Our Saudi scriptwriter develops Arabic scripts and branch maps; a MAGRABi coach and optometrist validate language, decisions and scoring before production.

5.2 Scenario anatomy

ModuleDecision pointsLearner timeLearning focus
M2 · Diagnose the Pain4–53–4 minDiscover the real pain beneath the initial request.
M3 · Differentiate the Claim5–6About 4 minChoose and communicate the claim that answers the identified pain.
M4 · Demonstrate the Gain6–74–5 minUse relevant proof, introduce price appropriately and respond to objections.
M5 · The Full Conversation8–10About 6 minComplete Pain–Claim–Gain conversation with greater complexity and no in-scenario prompts or feedback.

Each decision offers spoken response options. The selected answer triggers a customer reaction and concise feedback voice-over before the conversation continues, making the consequence visible. M5 assesses independent performance, with no prompts or in-conversation feedback.

5.3 Video production approach

All programme videos use AI-Generated Realistic Videos, maintaining consistent characters, wardrobe, voices and MAGRABi store environments across storylines. Platform compatibility and Saudi-dialect quality are validated in D.1.

5.4 Scenario banks, randomisation and retries

M2–M5 each use a four-scenario bank with randomized draws and encounter tracking. Retries prioritize unseen customers; after the bank is exhausted, learners complete targeted practice before another attempt. Retry caps and reset rules are confirmed in D.1; no additional scenario production is assumed.

5.5 Four recurring customer storylines

The four customers recur as learners build the skills to serve them. Their stories connect M2–M4 and converge in M5’s more demanding full-conversation assessment. The introductory video familiarizes learners with the characters without revealing their behaviours or the learning challenge.

5.6 Factor scoring

FactorWhat is assessedScoring approach
The PainQuality of questions, identification of the customer's pain and accurate reflection through the selected response.Highest weighting; its own pass floor applies.
The ClaimRelevance of the selected claim to the customer's pain, communicated as a meaningful contrast.Scored against the relevance of the claim to the identified pain.
The GainUse of proof before price and an appropriate response to the first objection.Scored against proof before price and the response to the first objection.

MAGRABi confirms factor weights, the Pain floor and composite threshold. Close remains part of the conversation—not a fourth scoring factor. MCQ choices map to validated ratings and consequences.

Weights, the Pain floor and the composite pass threshold are confirmed with MAGRABi in D.1. MCQ decisions replace the MCQ response; scoring is based on validated answer options and their mapped consequences.

GateBank sizePass requirementAssessment character
M24 scenarios2 of 4Pain discovery with guided feedback.
M34 scenarios2 of 4Pain and Claim, with reduced support.
M44 scenarios2 of 4Pain, Claim and Gain, with feedback after decisions.
M54 scenarios2 of 4*Full, more complex conversation without in-scenario prompts or feedback.

*M5's proposed 2-of-4 threshold is subject to MAGRABi approval because the RFQ currently specifies 3 of 4. The live practical assessment in M6 remains part of the certification journey.

From learning data to store performance

Performance support that keeps the learning alive.

Scenario results identify each employee’s strongest and weakest skills and direct the next practice, weekly manager coaching and daily huddles. The loop supports the live M6 assessment.

The performance-support loop
01 · INSIGHT
Individual Dashboard

Shows each employee's progress and skill profile across Pain, Claim and Gain.

02 · COACH
Weekly Manager Coaching

Focuses on the current module's priority skill, using employee results to guide the discussion.

03 · PRACTISE
Peer Role-Play

Turns the identified skill gap into a realistic, repeatable practice challenge.

04 · REINFORCE
Daily 10-Minute Huddles

Reinforces the same module skill through short, practical prompts linked to everyday behaviours.

The loop prepares learners for the next customer interaction and M6’s live assessment. Individual results guide development, not leaderboards.

Customer-in-the-Seat · Three-role peer practice

Roles rotate within the existing M5 two-hour peer role-play. The manager privately selects the Peer Instructor from learner results; no individual leaderboard is used.

Advisor

Leads the conversation and applies the skill being practised.

Customer

Plays the customer and introduces realistic questions, hesitation or resistance to make the conversation more challenging.

Peer Instructor

The strongest performer in the relevant skill observes, guides the debrief and shares effective approaches.

One customer, one advisor, one MAGRABi store, the same opening line. Three versions of about 90 seconds: transaction, feature, primal.

Method: AI-Generated Realistic Video. This is the first thing leadership and every new joiner sees, so it must feel like a credible MAGRABi store moment.

Three versions are written so that the camera, cast and opening stay identical and only the advisor's behaviour changes. The contrast does the teaching.

7. Technical solution

Learning runs in Absorb as SCORM 1.2, with video streamed through a content delivery network. Scenario interactions capture decisions and factor results; dashboard feasibility is confirmed with MAGRABi in D.1.

8.1 What sits inside and outside Absorb

ComponentWhereWhy
4 micro-modules (M1 to M4)Inside Absorb, one SCORM 1.2 package eachStandard tracking and completion
Scenario gates (M2 to M5)Inside Absorb, one SCORM 1.2 package per gate holding that module's bank, draw and retry logicCompletion and pass status flow to Absorb as normal
Scenario videoOutside: streamed from a content delivery network with adaptive qualityKeeps packages small and playback smooth on store Wi-Fi and mobile data
MCQ video-branching logicInside each scenario packageMaps each response to its authored customer reaction, feedback voice-over and factor score
Individual employee dashboard and manager viewAbsorb reporting where supported; otherwise a lightweight reporting layer subject to D.1 validationShows individual progress and Pain, Claim and Gain skill patterns to inform coaching and practice
Hero filmInside the M1 package and as a stand-alone Absorb video for the leadership rolloutReuse

8.2 Tracking, scoring and completion in SCORM 1.2

Completion: cmi.core.lesson_status is set to passed only when the learner passes the required number of drawn scenarios, each with The Pain above its floor and the composite above the threshold. Otherwise it stays incomplete or failed.

Score: cmi.core.score.raw carries the gate's composite score (0 to 100).

Factor scores: each scenario writes three cmi.interactions records (Pain, Claim, Gain) with the scenario ID, so the factor detail exists inside Absorb too.

Seen customers and retries: stored in cmi.suspend_data as short codes, well within the 4,096 character limit of SCORM 1.2.

D.1 validates whether Absorb can report learner progress and Pain, Claim and Gain patterns to employees and managers. If not, a lightweight external reporting layer is scoped before build.

Store-level leaderboards: built from the same factor data, by store only, never by individual, as the brief requires.

8.3 Randomisation, pooling and retry logic

Each gate randomizes draws from its four-scenario bank and tracks customer exposure. Retries prioritize unseen customers; once the bank is exhausted, targeted practice comes before another attempt. Retry caps, reset rules and reporting are confirmed in D.1.

8.4 Mobile and the 650 px player

Every screen is designed at 650 px visible height, landscape and portrait, with no scrolling inside a decision.

Tested on current iOS and Android phones, a tablet and a desktop browser, in Arabic and English, inside Absorb's modal player and the Absorb mobile app (if MAGRABi uses it).

Video starts within three seconds on a typical 4G connection; subtitles are on by default and can be switched off.
